doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Lead-in to the Shearing story and camera glare pause
summary: Toots offers to tell how he met Shearing; the crew adjusts the camera to avoid reflection.

story.theme_name: Tape changes, reel headers and session breaks
story.community_name: Tape changes, reel headers and session breaks

blocks.x: And then after that, George Shearing came to listen to me, and he sat backstage at the movie, you know. I met him then… Oh, but I have to tell you what happened.
Your chronology is fine. It’s the Toots’ version. Go ahead.
So then… I moved a little bit. Shall I come forward? Is it okay for you [inaudible]?
Uh, yeah. There’s some reflection in the sunglass. Maybe we should put it… try to put it down a little bit. Like this?
There’s a good reason for it. Struggling.
Yeah, we’ll have to hold it all the time. [laughs]
I think… I’m quite sure if you move a little bit to your left side, it will be better.
Yeah, are we gonna move it [a bit?]?
Yeah. From us, we can’t see the eyes. We got the reflection. It’s better.
Yeah. If he leans forward I can see that there’s no glare.
See if it’s okay for you.
